The Lost Coin
KOIN
noun phrase
From the Greek drachmē, a silver coin of a day’s wage; the parable of the woman who sweeps the house to find one piece of silver.

Biblical Definition

The parable of the Lost Coin is the companion of the Lost Sheep, and like it sets forth the diligent seeking of the lost and the joy that follows their recovery. Either what woman, said the LORD, having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it? And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost (Luk 15:8-9). And He gave the meaning: Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth (Luk 15:10). The dictionary marks this parable beside its fellow, the two teaching one truth under two figures. The sheep wanders abroad and is sought in the wilderness; the coin lies lost within the house, dark and unmindful of its own loss, and is sought by candle and broom till it be found. So the Scripture shows the sinner lost not only in open wandering but in dead and senseless insensibility, unable even to know himself lost; and it shows the diligence of the seeking grace that lights the candle, sweeps the house, and searches till the lost be found. The coin bears the image of its owner, marred and hidden in the dust, even as fallen man bears the defaced image of his Maker; and the joy of the finding is the joy of heaven, in the presence of the angels of God, over one sinner that repenteth.

Webster 1828 Definition

The parable in which a woman sweeps the house to find one lost coin, and rejoices with her neighbours when it is found.

expand to see more

THE LOST COIN, the parable of the woman seeking the lost piece of silver.

She lighteth a candle and sweepeth the house and seeketh diligently till she find it.

When she hath found it, she calleth her friends to rejoice with her.

There is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

The coin pictures the sinner lost in senseless insensibility, sought by grace.

Key Scripture

Luk 15:8 — "Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?"

Luk 15:9 — "And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost."

Luk 15:10 — "Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth."

Luk 19:10 — "For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost."

Modern Corruption

A parable of the kingdom teaching the diligent seeking of the lost and heaven’s joy over the penitent; it has drawn little redefinition.

expand to see more

The parable of the Lost Coin has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as the companion of the Lost Sheep in the LORD’s threefold answer to the murmuring of the Pharisees. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the candle lighted and the house swept till the lost coin be found.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the sinner is lost not only in open wandering but in dead and senseless insensibility, unable even to know himself lost, like a coin fallen in the dust. The seeking grace of God lights the candle, sweeps the house, and searches diligently till the lost be found; for the coin cannot seek itself. The defaced image upon the silver pictures the marred image of God in fallen man, recovered by Him who seeks it; and the joy of the finding is the joy of heaven, in the presence of the angels of God, over one sinner that repenteth.

Hebrew Roots

From the Greek drachmē, a silver coin, the parable names the woman who seeks the lost piece till she find it.
